sq.QUESTION_DESC: The nodes of the list are given by 23, 34, 46, 57 and 68. Insert a new node with the data 17 before the node 57 and the data 77 at the end of the list. The predecessor and successor nodes of 77 are 68 and 23 respectively. Demonstrate the insertion operation with suitable pseudo code.

lq.ANSWER:
#include <stdio.h>

#include <stdlib.h>

 

// Node structure

struct Node {

    int data;

    struct Node* next;

};

 

// Insert at the beginning

void insertAtBeginning(struct Node** head, int value) {

    struct Node* newNode = (struct Node*)malloc(sizeof(struct Node));

    newNode->data = value;

 

    if (*head == NULL) {

        newNode->next = newNode;

        *head = newNode;

    } else {

        struct Node* temp = *head;

        while (temp->next != *head) {

            temp = temp->next;

        }

        newNode->next = *head;

        temp->next = newNode;

        *head = newNode;

    }

 

    printf("Inserted %d at the beginning.\n", value);

}

 

// Insert at the end

void insertAtEnd(struct Node** head, int value) {

    struct Node* newNode = (struct Node*)malloc(sizeof(struct Node));

    newNode->data = value;

 

    if (*head == NULL) {

        newNode->next = newNode;

        *head = newNode;

    } else {

        struct Node* temp = *head;

        while (temp->next != *head) {

            temp = temp->next;

        }

        temp->next = newNode;

        newNode->next = *head;

    }

 

    printf("Inserted %d at the end.\n", value);

}

 

// Insert at a specific position

void insertAtPosition(struct Node** head, int value, int position) {

    if (position == 1) {

        insertAtBeginning(head, value);

        return;

    }

 

    struct Node* newNode = (struct Node*)malloc(sizeof(struct Node));

    newNode->data = value;

 

    struct Node* temp = *head;

    for (int i = 1; i < position - 1; i++) {

        temp = temp->next;

        if (temp == *head) {

            printf("Position out of bounds.\n");

            free(newNode);

            return;

        }

    }

 

    newNode->next = temp->next;

    temp->next = newNode;

    printf("Inserted %d at position %d.\n", value, position);

}

 

// Display circular list

void display(struct Node* head) {

    if (head == NULL) {

        printf("List is empty.\n");

        return;

    }

 

    struct Node* temp = head;

    printf("Circular List: ");

    do {

        printf("%d -> ", temp->data);

        temp = temp->next;

    } while (temp != head);

    printf("(back to head)\n");

}

 

// Main driver

int main() {

    struct Node* head = NULL;

 

    insertAtEnd(&head, 10);

    insertAtBeginning(&head, 5);

    insertAtEnd(&head, 20);

    insertAtPosition(&head, 15, 3);

 

    display(head);  // Expected: 5 -> 10 -> 15 -> 20 -> (back to head)

 

    return 0;

}

Circular playlist ensures infinite looping of songs without needing to restart manually.
lq.QUESTION_DESC:
You are developing a music player app where songs are played in a loop. To achieve this, you use a circular singly linked list where each node stores the song ID.

  • When a user starts the playlist, the first song is inserted at the beginning.
  • When new songs are added to the end of the playlist, they should be appended such that the last song still links back to the first.
  • Users can also insert a favorite song at a specific position in the playlist (e.g., between song 2 and song 3).
  • The playlist must remain circular after every operation.

Task:
Write a program in C to:

  1. Insert a song at the beginning
  2. Insert a song at the end
  3. Insert a song at a given position
  4. Display the playlist in a circular fashion

Also explain why a circular structure is preferred in this scenario.
